newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Edgars year earnings seen flat.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Edgars year earnings seen flat.

text.p: South African fashion chain Edgars Stores Ltd is set to post flat full year earnings, reined in by a slowdown in consumer spending and tough trading conditions in the credit retail sector.
The group, which is scheduled to post year results on Tuesday, reported disappointing first-half results in November with margins down and sales barely ahead of inflation.

It said at the time it anticipated difficult trading conditions to continue through at least the first half of 1997, citing an unfavourable economic climate and high levels of consumer debt and interest rates.

Analysts polled by Reuters expected full year earnings to come in little changed at 638 cent per share from 642 cents at the 1996 year-end, while the final dividend was expected flat at 247 cents. But they said that overstocking problems in subsidiary Jet Stores appeared remedied.
"We're looking at the same fundamentals as the first half which was down by about seven percent," Simpson Mckie-James Capel analyst John Biccard said.
"But the second half of last year was loss making for Jet Stores and the group should be in a better position in the second half of this year, helping earnings for the full year," he added.

Another analyst who asked not to be named agreed that the overstocking problems at Jet -- which hampered previous year results -- had been overcome, therefore leading to an improvement over first half results.
She also said credit tightening measures at Jet and better handling of the sales book were positive signs.
"Generally the company (Jet) is now much more wary about issuing credit than they were in the past," the analyst noted.

But while earnings in the second half were expected to show an improvement over the first half, difficult trading conditions in the credit retail sector would ensure flat year earnings growth, analysts agreed.
"The credit bubble has burst and that's affecting consumers considerably," one noted.

Another underlined those sentiments: "The bottomline this year is that earnings are expected to be unchanged because September 1996 was the anniversary of extended credit for (units) Sales House and Edgars."

In the half year results to end September, attributable income at Edgars Stores fell five percent at 145.1 million rand. The company said retail sales of 2,659.9 million rand versus 2,318.9 million rand a year earlier were below expectations.
